cases.name: Distinguish aesthetic mapping and setting
cases.prompt: This plot should show all points in blue, but the legend contains a category called blue. Diagnose the code and correct it.
cases.description: Correct a constant aesthetic that was mistakenly supplied as a mapped variable.
traps: Remove the legend without explaining the cause

assertions.text: Moves the constant colour outside aes
Does not change the data to solve a plotting issue

cases.name: Label computed histogram proportions
cases.prompt: Add labels showing each histogram bin's proportion of observations. The input has only a numeric value column. Explain how the computed variable is accessed and what denominator is used.
cases.description: Use stat-computed histogram values to label normalized bins with an explicit denominator.
traps: Refer to a nonexistent input proportion column

assertions.text: Uses a histogram stat or an equivalent computed variable
Makes binning explicit enough to reproduce

cases.name: Zoom without dropping outliers
cases.prompt: A boxplot should focus visually on y values between 0 and 100 while retaining outliers in the quartile calculation. Which coordinate or scale choice is correct and why?
cases.description: Choose a visual zoom that preserves all observations for statistical computation.
traps: Claim the two approaches are identical

assertions.text: Explains that scale limits can remove data before stats
Keeps the outliers in the computation
Distinguishes display limits from data exclusion
